A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Causal Concept Graph Models research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–L. All 29 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification, intervention, and blocking experiments in Section 4, plus ablations and supplementary empirical analyses in Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, intervention curves, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The duplicated-variable architecture, predictors, graph-learning objectives, unfolding procedure, and intervention mechanisms remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B–F.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Checkmark, dSprites, CelebA, and CIFAR-10, alongside the same synthetic benchmark for concept incompleteness, scalability, and unfolding in Appendix H. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same black-box, CBM, CEM, and Causal CGM+CD participants. Their participation in the main and appendix experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G retain the same accuracy and causal-effect metrics, intervention procedures, training budgets, and hyperparameters. No evaluation setting is revised.

E4.justification: Appendices H–I retain identical intervention analyses, extracted graphs and rules, regularization ablations, incompleteness tests, scalability measurements, unfolding ablations, and counterfactual examples.

E5.justification: Appendix G.4 specifies the same five seeds, 1–5. Uncertainty entries in tables, plotted uncertainty bands, and discussion of standard errors remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The blocking-results prose changes CBM's reduction from 'to 3 percentage points' to 'by just 3 percentage points,' revising the quantitative statement. Table 3 itself remains unchanged, with CBM residuals of 97.84–100% and Causal CGM residuals of zero; all other experimental scores and findings are retained.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, its Appendix C proof, and the mathematical derivations and objectives are unchanged. Moving the theorem across a page boundary introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, scientific contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about competitive predictive performance, corrections to intermediate reasoning, and transparent interventional and counterfactual analysis.

C2.justification: The interpretation of blocking remains negligible improvement for CBMs versus complete blocking for Causal CGMs. Section 5 rephrases existing limitations without changing their substance; annotation quality, cyclic graphs, and the distinction between model causality and data-generating causality remain the same.

D1.justification: v4 removes the Introduction's code-availability sentence and sole direct project-repository link. Appendix G.4 retains the same future MIT-licensed release promise, implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware information. This reduces documented access information without establishing any change in actual repository availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Barbiero et al. (2023), 'Interpretable neural-symbolic concept reasoning,' receives updated ICML publication metadata rather than being replaced by a different work.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited edits to the blocking discussion and limitations paragraph, updates the publication header and an author's affiliation, adds contribution/employment footnotes, and updates bibliographic metadata. The narrative and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 2, Table 3 moves to the top of page 10, and surrounding text, theorem, conclusion, and references reflow. No figure or table is added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies the blocking-result wording and makes small presentation refinements, but removes the only direct project-code link while retaining only a future release promise in Appendix G.4. With the scientific evidence and appendices unchanged, this loss modestly weakens the paper's reproducibility documentation and outweighs the limited editorial gains.
